identityReview: Irene Khan / Irene Zubaida Khan, human-rights advocate and diplomat from Bangladesh. National Portrait Gallery supports 1956 and Dhaka; year-only birth is retained. Roles are distinguished: Amnesty Secretary General August 2001–31 December 2009, IDLO Director-General 1 January 2012–end 2019, first female freedom-of-expression Special Rapporteur 1 August 2020–31 July 2026, and Bangladesh’s Permanent Representative with credentials presented 28 August 2026. Do not continue her former independent UN mandate as a current concurrent role or treat national diplomatic representation as employment by the UN Secretariat.
lifeStatusEvidence: The UN’s 4 November 2026 protocol list records Khan’s 28 August presentation of credentials, corroborated by the contemporaneous bdnews24 account of the completed New York meeting with António Guterres. The mission’s indexed 5 November General Assembly statement is additional recent authorship/role evidence, not verified video or proof of physical speech delivery. No event image or recording was reviewed.

sourceReview.accessMethod: Read NPG biography; relevant 2007 Amnesty career passages; short IDLO 2014 biography; relevant 2019 succession and current successor biography passages; Sydney laureate citation; 2011 committee departure/payment breakdown; the December independent-review response; ARTICLE 19 end-of-tenure release; Graduate Institute profile; UN protocol Bangladesh entry and dated footers; bdnews24 event account; and indexed mission statement title. Commons permission/history was read, but primary licence recovery and pixels remain unavailable.
corrections: Read the National Portrait Gallery sitter biography, which identifies Irene Zubaida Khan, gives birth year 1956 and Dhaka, and describes childhood in East Pakistan before Bangladesh’s 1971 independence. It supports teenage schooling in Northern Ireland and law study at Manchester and Harvard. The title Secretary General describes her historical portrait identity, not her current 2026 office. Retain year-only birth precision: the widely repeated 24 December day was not independently established in the authoritative biography. Do not confuse the 1971 independence war with her birth year or infer an earned doctorate from honorary titles.

Read the relevant 2007 Amnesty biography, ORG 10/001/2007. It explicitly gives August 2001 for her appointment as seventh Secretary General, first woman/Asian/Muslim in that position, expansion into economic/social/cultural rights, and the March 2004 campaign against violence toward women. It also records UNHCR entry in 1980, India mission leadership in 1995, the 1999 Kosovo-crisis team in the then Former Yugoslav Republic of Macedonia, and later 1999 deputy directorship for international protection. She was not UN High Commissioner herself. The PDF’s 2021 hosting path is not the original biography date, and institutional praise or lists of missions do not establish independently measured results.

Read the concise IDLO biography dated November 2014. Member Parties elected her on 17 November 2011; she formally took office on 1 January 2012, as IDLO’s first female Director-General. These dates correct shorthand accounts that place the election in January 2012. The initial four-year term is not the whole eventual eight-year tenure. Its old current titles and board positions are not automatically current in November 2026. Harvard/Manchester study and the 2006 Sydney award are corroborated, without invented graduation years or degree labels.

Read the 13 November 2019 succession announcement’s election and end-of-term passages. It says Khan’s final term ends at the end of 2019 and Jan Beagle was elected successor, expected to begin in January 2020. The successor’s current official biography separately confirms actual accession on 1 January. Do not treat 13 November 2019, the election date, as the handover day. Organisational programme counts in the release were not independently audited and are not presented as Khan’s personal outputs.

Read the Sydney Peace Foundation’s 2006 laureate heading and award citation. It recognises human-rights leadership and making violence against women a central injustice in peace advocacy. This is the Sydney Peace Prize, not a Nobel award. The source reviewed supports the year; no precise ceremony day, prize amount or independent evaluation of all campaigning effects is invented. Her Secretary General title belongs to the award’s 2006 context.

Read the Executive Committee’s 2011 letter through its leadership-change rationale, negotiated departure and payment breakdown. It says leadership change was discussed in 2008, she disagreed, and an agreement ended employment on 31 December 2009. The £533103 paid in the year to 31 March 2010 includes ordinary salary/pension/overtime, backdated pay, earlier bonuses and allowances; the termination-related component is £191697, not the whole total. Payments to Kate Gilmore are separate. The committee’s employment-law explanation is its account, not an independently reviewed legal judgment or proof of criminal wrongdoing.

Read Amnesty’s 1 December 2011 announcement and relevant reform passages following Dame Anne Owers’s independent review. Amnesty accepted findings/recommendations and acknowledged management and governance failures leading to excessive payments to Khan and Gilmore. This later institutional acknowledgment is distinguished from the earlier committee letter’s defence of its decision. The original full review and underlying employment agreement were not obtained. The statement does not establish an individual criminal conviction; the PDF hosting date in 2021 is not the 2011 announcement date.

Read ARTICLE 19’s 31 July 2026 conclusion-of-tenure release. Its dated present-tense conclusion and six-year description establish the end of the 2020–2026 mandate; it names Khan as the first woman appointed and reviews themes including women, disinformation, conflict information, development, exiled journalists and Big Tech. The attached caption dates a photograph to 17 October 2022 and is not a new July 2026 appearance. Praise and impact assessments are ARTICLE 19’s institutional evaluation, not an audit of every country communication or result.

Read the Geneva Graduate Institute profile, which gives the mandate start as 1 August 2020 and lists The Unheard Truth: Poverty and Human Rights (Norton, 2009). It corroborates prior Amnesty/IDLO roles and legal/public-policy background. Its present-tense Special Rapporteur wording is stale after the July 2026 end and is explicitly superseded. No full book was read or exact thesis attributed. Its university chancellorship dates are not adopted because a Salford succession page gives a different appointment chronology; no unsupported professor/chancellor current title is retained.

Read the Bangladesh entry and dated footers of the UN Protocol and Liaison Service heads-of-mission PDF. The document is dated 4 November 2026 and names Irene Zubaida Khan with presentation of credentials on 28 August 2026. This supports current national diplomatic office and the credential milestone, not an independent UN expert mandate or a UN Secretariat appointment. The list itself does not supply her full career or the exact date of her domestic appointment.

Read bdnews24.com’s 29 August 2026 report, updated 8 September, through the credentials, appointment and career passages. It records actual presentation to António Guterres in New York on Friday and a 8 July appointment; the UN list independently confirms 28 August. August 29 is the article date, not the credential date. The article relies on a mission statement for the event. Its residual present-perfect Special Rapporteur wording is corrected using the end-of-tenure record. Its broad faculty description is not used to infer a current professorship.

Read the mission’s indexed title naming Khan as Permanent Representative in the General Assembly debate on the ECOSOC report on 5 November 2026, plus the mission news index showing publication on 6 November. The original page timed out, so the full speech, exact wording, policy positions and physical delivery were not independently reviewed. This is recent published statement-record evidence, while the August credential event provides a separately documented actual activity. Do not turn the 6 November upload into a different event date.

Read IDLO’s current Director-General biography opening. It explicitly confirms Jan Beagle was elected on 13 November 2019 and formally took office on 1 January 2020, later re-elected in November 2023. This confirms actual succession after the earlier prospective release and prevents carrying Khan’s old IDLO title forward. Beagle’s subsequent tenure, work and achievements are not attributed to Khan.

additionalConsulted.access: Read the 21 March 2011 report of Khan’s lawyers’ clarification: payments included income owed for previous years and different purposes, rather than remuneration earned solely in one year. Its approximate £532000 wording does not replace the committee’s itemised £533103 total. The linked original solicitor letter was not read.

sourceReview.limits: AI editorial and translation review, not certified native-language human review. No birth certificate, exact birthday verification, academic credential, full book, full Owers review, original settlement agreement, audited case-by-case mandate outcomes, complete November speech, event recording or portrait pixels were inspected. Distinguish historical offices, current diplomacy, election/appointment/accession dates, payment totals and their components, institutional reviews and court findings. Refresh current roles and obtain a verified reusable original-colour portrait before publication.

translationReview.scope: All 32 display fields in seven foreign languages reviewed against Chinese and English. Preserve year-only 1956 birth and Dhaka/East Pakistan context; law study versus honorary doctorate; August 2001 seventh Amnesty Secretary General and first woman/Asian/Muslim in that office; 2004 campaign; Sydney versus Nobel prize; negotiated 31 December 2009 departure; £533103 fiscal-year payments including arrears versus £191697 termination component; institutional review versus criminal conviction; 2011 IDLO election versus January 2012 accession and January 2020 successor; 1 August 2020–31 July 2026 independent mandate versus national diplomatic representation from 28 August; 4 November protocol date versus 5 November statement and 6 November publication.
